build.name: Companion Spirit Walker
build.seoTitle: PoE2 Companion Spirit Walker Build Guide 0.5.5 | Lv1 to Endgame Leveling
build.seoDescription: PoE2 0.5.5: Companion Spirit Walker — raising a Tame Beast companion, the Act 3 setup switch, gear and passives by stage. Enter your current level to see the three things to do now.

reviewedFacts.ssfNote: There is an SSF guide for the early game through Early Endgame. Maxroll (0.5.5) explicitly states no uniques are required. Whether the Endgame setup works in SSF is unconfirmed.

strengths: There is a clear Endgame plan built around a unique beast as the main damage dealer.
The Act 1–3 leveling route and the conditions for switching to the companion setup are explained.
Simple operation: Maxroll (0.5.5) introduces it as a very simple playstyle where you can sit back and let your minions do the job.
The companion draws enemy attention and soaks attacks, so you can focus on positioning and staying safe (PoE Vault).

Maxroll (0.5.5) explicitly states the build works without any unique items. However, it does not explicitly call it SSF-viable, and it notes that the method of pausing with the Marketplace hotkey to check the beast's abilities in maps cannot be used in SSF.
Odealo (0.5.0) lists 'easy to play', 'high damage' and 'high survivability' as PROS, and explains that the Mighty Silverfist in Act 3 solves the lack of boss damage.
weaknesses: Tame Beast is a Tier 7 gem, so it cannot be used early on; switching to the companion setup is recommended in Act 3, after the second trial.
You need to keep gold aside for the respec from the Twister setup to the companion setup.
After the switch, clearing is slower than the early Twister playstyle (PoE Vault).
The Endgame version has somewhat low durability early on, and you need to watch your positioning (PoE Vault).
Finding the optimal boss companion (an individual with good mods) requires farming. However, this is only about pushing the build to its absolute limit (PoE Vault).
A boss companion is poor at clearing large packs, its attacks are slow and its aim is rough. Minion AI can also cause problems (Odealo).

levelingStages.label: Lv1–10
levelingStages.supports: Whirling Slash: Rage, Rapid Attacks. Twister: Retreat, Chilling Ice.
levelingStages.passivePriority: Do not lean into the companion setup early; use the source's per-stage Act 1 tree.
levelingStages.gearPriority: Added damage on spear, gloves and rings, Life, resistances.
levelingStages.replaceGear: Prioritize replacing a spear with low added damage.
levelingStages.caution: Do not switch to the companion setup at this stage.
levelingStages.transitionCondition: Reach Lv11. Progress steadily with Twister and Whirling Slash.
nowActions: Progress with Twister and Whirling Slash
Check the added damage on your spear, gloves and rings
Do not spend all the gold you are saving for the respec

levelingStages.label: Lv11–20
levelingStages.supports: Continue the Act 1 setup and move on to the source's per-stage Act 2 setup. Check any unconfirmed slots in the source.
levelingStages.passivePriority: Use the source's per-stage Act 2 tree, and do not respec into the finished companion setup yet.
levelingStages.gearPriority: Added damage on spear, gloves and rings, movement speed, Life, resistances.
levelingStages.replaceGear: Apart from early weapon upgrades, do not overspend gold; keep funds for the Act 3 switch.
levelingStages.caution: Gambling purchases in Acts 2–3 can easily eat into your switch funds, so hold back.
levelingStages.transitionCondition: Reach Lv21. Aim for the Tier 7 gem and the second trial.
nowActions: Continue the Twister leveling
Check movement speed and resistances
Keep gold saved for the switch

levelingStages.label: Lv21–30
levelingStages.mainSkill: Twister + Whirling Slash until you finish the second trial in Act 3. After preparing a level 7 Tame Beast gem and the respec, move to the Act 3 SWAP. A candidate is the Mighty Silverfist in Act 3.
levelingStages.supports: For companion supports, check the source's Act 3 SWAP stage. Do not state names that cannot be extracted reliably.
levelingStages.passivePriority: After the second trial, respec everything at once into the source's per-stage Act 3 SWAP tree.
levelingStages.gearPriority: Companion damage, minion skill levels, Life, Evasion / Deflection, resistances.
levelingStages.replaceGear: After the switch, gradually update from spear-focused gear to companion gear.
levelingStages.caution: The source recommends switching in Act 3, after the second trial. Do not switch on level alone; check the level 7 Tame Beast gem and the funds for the passive respec.
levelingStages.transitionCondition: The Tier 7 gem, the second trial, and the respec funds are all in place.
nowActions: Finish the second trial
Prepare the Tier 7 gem
Keep switch funds saved and move to the companion setup

levelingStages.label: Lv31–40
levelingStages.mainSkill: Use a unique companion you have obtained as your main damage dealer, such as the Mighty Silverfist in the Jungle Ruins of Act 3, which the source names as a single-target candidate. The source explains that other unique companions can also progress.
levelingStages.supports: Check the companion setup you chose in the source's Skill Gems → Act 3 SWAP. Do not carry the spear leveling supports over to the companion as-is.
levelingStages.passivePriority: Use the per-stage companion tree after the Act 3 SWAP.
levelingStages.gearPriority: Companion damage, minion attack speed, minion gem levels, Life, Evasion, resistances.
levelingStages.replaceGear: Replace spear leveling gear that does not help the companion, starting with pieces that help the companion and your defense.
levelingStages.caution: Companions differ by type, but do not declare an unconfirmed individual mandatory or the strongest.
levelingStages.transitionCondition: Reach Lv41. The companion, as the main damage dealer, can handle regular enemies and strong enemies.
nowActions: Complete the switch to the companion tree
Swap to gear that helps the companion, one piece at a time
Check the companion's AI and positioning

levelingStages.label: Lv41–Campaign End
levelingStages.mainSkill: Continue with the companion as the main damage dealer, while you guide enemies and keep a safe position.
levelingStages.supports: Use the source's per-stage Act 4 and Interludes setups in order.
levelingStages.passivePriority: Progress from Act 4 to the per-stage Interludes tree, connecting into the mapping setup.
levelingStages.gearPriority: Life, Evasion / Deflection, elemental resistances, companion damage, minion attack speed.
levelingStages.replaceGear: If you die often, prioritize your own armor and resistances over companion damage.
levelingStages.caution: The companion can get stuck in corridors. In narrow places, move yourself to guide it.
levelingStages.transitionCondition: Campaign finished. Companion uptime, your own defense and positioning are stable.
nowActions: Sort out your own Life and resistances
Guide the companion in narrow places
Check the per-stage Interludes tree

levelingStages.label: Early Maps
levelingStages.mainSkill: Use the unique companion you have obtained as your main damage dealer. If you value single target, the Mighty Silverfist is the source's candidate. In maps, also check the AI and how it moves through corridors.
levelingStages.supports: Progress to the source's pre-Red Maps stage. Cross-check companion-specific supports against the tame target and the current guide.
levelingStages.passivePriority: Move to the companion / defense tree for the start of mapping.
levelingStages.gearPriority: Elemental and chaos resistances, Life, Evasion / Deflection, companion damage, minion gem levels.
levelingStages.replaceGear: If you get killed in low-Tier maps, check your armor; if clearing is slow, check gear that helps the companion.
levelingStages.caution: Check the companion's type and granted effects. The source names the Mighty Silverfist for single target, and as an example of a rare individual, a Plague Harvester with a defensive effect such as Temporal Bubble. The latter's effect is not fixed, so check it per individual.
levelingStages.transitionCondition: In low-Tier maps, the companion's survival and your own defense are stable.
nowActions: Check elemental and chaos resistances
Watch the companion's survival and AI
Work out whether the shortfall is defense or companion damage

levelingStages.label: Early Endgame
levelingStages.mainSkill: If you value single target, the source's Mighty Silverfist. Other unique companions also work, so choose by what you actually obtain and how manageable the AI is.
levelingStages.supports: Progress from Red Maps to the per-stage Endgame setup. Do not mix in supports that do not fit the tame target.
levelingStages.passivePriority: Follow the per-stage trees in the order Red Maps, then Endgame.
levelingStages.gearPriority: Companion damage, minion attack speed, minion gem levels, ES, Evasion, defense, resistances.
levelingStages.replaceGear: Make the later ES transition one piece at a time while keeping resistances and actual defense.
levelingStages.caution: A Rare Werewolf with Haste and similar are candidates, but check the abilities of the individual you obtained before adopting it.
levelingStages.transitionCondition: The companion's role, supports and the purpose of the defense transition are clear.
nowActions: Check the companion's abilities on the actual individual
Follow the per-stage Red Maps tree
Make the ES transition one piece at a time

levelingStages.label: Endgame
levelingStages.mainSkill: In the source's Endgame version, the Mighty Silverfist is the candidate for single target. In other setups such as the Zoo version, arrange support, defense and positioning around the companion you adopted.
levelingStages.supports: Choose the source setup for the Endgame or Zoo stage and match it to the tame target and gear assumptions.
levelingStages.passivePriority: Do not mix Endgame and Zoo; use the per-stage tree you chose as the base and adjust for missing defense.
levelingStages.gearPriority: Companion damage, minion attack speed, minion gem levels, ES, Evasion / Deflection, resistances.
levelingStages.replaceGear: Do not use fixed prices or DPS; only update pieces that address a shortfall for you or your companion.
levelingStages.caution: Do not treat the Mighty Silverfist as the only correct answer for every situation. The companion's body-blocking and AI remain weaknesses. Check single-target damage and ease of use while clearing separately.
levelingStages.transitionCondition: Once finished, improve companion damage, your own defense and AI countermeasures one item at a time.
nowActions: Decide on the Endgame or Zoo direction
Check your own and your companion's shortfalls separately
Adjust AI and positioning in actual combat

gearPriorities: Weapon for the first half of leveling (until the Act 3 switch): increased / added physical damage, accuracy and critical strike chance on the spear. Gloves and rings take added damage (PoE Vault).
Weapon after the switch: Sceptre + shield. On the sceptre, prioritize '+ levels to minion skills' and 'Allies in your Presence deal increased Damage' (Maxroll 0.5.5).
Helmet and amulet: + levels to minion skills. Start looking for the helmet and sceptre from Act 2 (PoE Vault).
Shield, chest, gloves, boots: maximum Life and resistances. PoE Vault's Endgame version is Evasion-based, and aims for 'gain Deflection equal to a portion of your Evasion' on gloves and boots.
At the start of mapping: secure 75% elemental resistances (chaos resistance is good to have). When you change gear, do not drop below the resistance caps or required attributes (Maxroll / PoE Vault).

Endgame main hand: with the ascendancy The Catha's Balance, the main-hand weapon's damage is added to the companion, so use the unique Tyranny's Grip (or Trenchtimbre for a more durable option) upgraded with a Verisium Anvil. The build also works without uniques (Maxroll 0.5.5).
Rings and belt: Breach-crafted minion mods are also effective, but meet required attributes and resistances first (PoE Vault).

sources.type: Japanese strategy reference (updated September 18, 2026. Referenced for strengths / weaknesses and recommended gear)

build.audience: Players who want a companion as their main damage dealer and can enjoy a major setup change partway through leveling

beginner.note: Only the conditions that were counted are tied to the source guides. The main skill, Tame Beast, is a Tier 7 gem so it cannot be used from the early game, and SSF has not been confirmed through to the Endgame setup, so those are not counted as confirmed conditions.

moderateOperation.basis: Maxroll (0.5.5, updated September 17, 2026) states in its introduction: 'a very simple playstyle where you can sit back and let your minions do the job for you'

noDodgeRequirement.basis: PoE Vault's Strengths state 'Minions take agro and block incoming attacks' and 'You can focus on positioning and safety while your minions deal damage'

damage.sourceName: Odealo: Tame Unique Beast Spirit Walker POE 2 Build
damage.note: The PROS list high damage with an emphasizing word. The source is for 0.5.0 (created June 4, 2026) and is a setup built around the Mighty Silverfist.

defense.basis: Both a strength and a weakness
defense.quote: Starts off a little weak defensively, so requires more defensive positioning
defense.sourceName: PoE Vault: Spiritwalker Boss Companion Endgame Build
defense.note: The quote describes PoE Vault's note on weak defense at the start of Endgame. It does not mean durability stays uniformly low through finished gear. A cited CaptainLance9 guide lists durability as a strength, and Odealo also lists survivability as a strength, so read it separated by leveling / gear stage and setup.

mapping.quote: Will be a bit slower than the Twister playstyle that you start with
mapping.sourceName: PoE Vault: Spiritwalker Companion Leveling Build
mapping.note: The Weaknesses state that clearing becomes slower than the early Twister playstyle.

boss.quote: Your Unique Companion solves any problems with your Damage against other Bosses, but it struggles with clearing hordes of weaker enemies.
boss.sourceName: Odealo: Tame Unique Beast Spirit Walker POE 2 Build
boss.note: The build overview text explains boss damage as a strength, contrasted with the weakness of clearing packs (a statement in the body text, not the PROS list; there is no emphasizing word, so it is rated 4). Gamerch's star rating is 'Bossing ★★☆', but it is not a written strength / weakness, so it is not used for scoring.

changeHistory.summary: Checked Odealo (0.5.0) and Gamerch (updated September 18). Updated damage from unrated to 5/5 (the PROS 'Great Damage') and boss from unrated to 4/5 (the body text stating it solves insufficient boss damage). Added strengths / weaknesses and sources.

Rechecked Maxroll (0.5.5 update) and PoE Vault. Added 'simple operation' and 'safe positioning' as confirmed conditions for the beginner rating (3/5), detailed gear priorities by slot, and added strengths / weaknesses and sources. Damage and boss remained unrated as there was no supporting statement.

Specified the Mighty Silverfist in the Jungle Ruins named by the source, examples of rare individuals' effects, and the switch conditions after the second trial in Act 3. Details of per-individual supports are to be checked in the adopted source stage.

Rechecked the source statements, target stages and source information, and fixed mix-ups and over-generalizations. Sources and dynamic setups that could not be confirmed are not treated as re-verified, and the overall leveling check date has not been changed.

Rechecked the publication status, supported patch, update date, main skill and ascendancy of 5 of the 7 sources, and updated the check dates. The two Mobalytics sources could not be fetched automatically, so they remain unchecked (check dates left as-is).
